channel.description: Approved local stories in broadcast order

item.description: Heating oil prices in Vermont have soared by up to eighty percent, hitting towns and schools hard. Many areas now pay over six dollars per gallon, double last year's cost. School districts face budget shortfalls of more than one hundred thirty thousand dollars due to these rising fuel costs.
Election Day is Tuesday, November third, and Vermont voters should be ready. Absentee ballots must be returned by seven p.m., and polling places will be open statewide.

A multi-vehicle crash on Interstate Eighty-Nine southbound near mile marker one-oh-four caused major traffic delays Thursday morning. Franklin County fire crews responded quickly to the scene. Drivers should expect continued delays in that area.

Rutland City voters will decide on a new capital reserve fund for school improvements. The fund won't raise taxes but will help cover building repairs and upgrades. An informational meeting is set for November second ahead of Election Day.
